Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call .
Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA-I for the State contends that the police authorities in compliance of the directions issued by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 46998 of 2020 (Junaid Vs State of U.P. and another) reported at 2021 (6) ADJ 511 and with a view to implement the provisions of POCSO Act, 2012 read with POCSO Rules, 2020, have served the bail application upon the victim/legal guardian as well as upon the CWC.
By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
32 of 2024 at Police Station- Belaghat District- Gorakhpur under Sections 376(2)N, 452, 504, 506 IPC and Section 5/6L of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 13.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Chandra Bhushan Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Neeraj Tiwari, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 15 years age in the prosecution case only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no legal basis for age related entries in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 16 years are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 16 years of age.
3. The applicant and the victim were intimate.
4. The victim and the applicant were found in a compromising position at the house of the victim.
5. The applicant came to the house of the victim at her invite for a lovers' tryst.
6. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to calling the applicant to her house at the dead night.
False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim at the behest of her parents in the latter part of the aforesaid statement to save the failing prosecution case.
7. The victim has not made any allegation of commission of rape, abduction or forceful assault against the applicant in her statement under Section 164 CrPC.
8. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
9. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.

sentences.text: The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
11. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Abhay Yadav be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
